speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: But he has WhatsApp records that e2i messaged him on 15 December, asking him if he was still looking for work and he replied "yes" on the same day.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: He followed up on 24 December, asking about jobs with hours compatible with sending his children to school.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: And as far as I can tell, e2i did not respond to either messages.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: So, without pre-judging things, my question is, does SSO take e2i's or other employment partner agencies' word, unconditionally, before rejecting an applicant for non-engagement?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Is the applicants given a chance to present their side?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: I will say this: for each family and each applicant, they face various unique circumstances and challenges.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: And actually, for this particular family, it is a known family and the family coach has helped the family in other ways as well, including provision of food rations, infant milk powder and diapers.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: Having said that, this cessation of financial assistance or the tapering off of it, is not something that SSO takes very lightly.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: SSO reviews it with the help of the Social Assistance Officer (SAO), who has embarked and partnered with the applicant family on the action plan, which would help them to improve their financial situation.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: And so, the SAO will contact the applicants for an interview and at the stage of assessment of the SMTA, the SAO will also get information from the family coach, from other sources of information as well, to ensure that they look at the entire assistance that is required by the family.

And rest assured, for the Member, that every applicant for SMTA will be able to get financial assistance by SSOs and we will look at how to help them meet their basic living needs and also journey with them on this journey for self-reliance so that they can improve their financial situation.
That is the purpose of the action plan.

I ask all Members in this House, if they know of any residents or they know of any applicants, partner with the SSOs so that we can embark on this action plan with them together on the path towards self-reliance, not just financial assistance.
